title: Bumrah Was Rested for Ireland and England. He Was Not Rested for the Asian Games.
excerpt: India have named a full-strength squad for the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, with Jasprit Bumrah spearheading the bowling attack and 15-year-old Sooryavanshi in all three squads.
body:
India have named their strongest-ever cricket squad for the Asian Games, and the headline act is not the new captain. It is the bowler who was nowhere near the other squads announced on the same day.

Jasprit Bumrah — rested for the upcoming T20I tours of Ireland and England — has been picked for the 2026 Asian Games in Japan this September. The selection panel, led by Ajit Agarkar, met in Mumbai on Saturday and announced four separate squads in one sitting: the T20I squad for Ireland and England, the Asian Games fifteen, and the India A side for multi-day matches in Sri Lanka. Bumrah's name appeared in exactly one of those lists.

## A Rest, Then a Reset

The reasoning is straightforward. Bumrah has had a relentless 12 months. The World Test Championship cycle, the home season, the IPL — his workload has been among the highest of any fast bowler in international cricket. The selectors have opted to give him the Ireland and England window off entirely, then bring him back for what is, in cricketing terms, a relatively low-intensity tournament.

Cricket at the Asian Games will be played in the T20 format, with the main event running from September 24 to October 3 at the Korogi Athletic Park in Aichi-Nagoya. India enter as defending champions after winning gold in Hangzhou in 2022, when a second-string squad under Ruturaj Gaikwad got the job done. This time, the BCCI has decided there will be no underestimating the opposition.

## Iyer Leads a New-Look Side

Shreyas Iyer, freshly appointed as India's T20I captain after replacing Suryakumar Yadav, will lead the Asian Games squad. Tilak Varma is his vice-captain. The fifteen-man squad reads like a starting XI plus reserves for a World Cup, not a multi-sport event: Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan as the two wicketkeepers, Abhishek Sharma and Shivam Dube providing left-handed firepower, Washington Sundar and Axar Patel offering spin-bowling all-rounder depth, and a pace attack of Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, and Harshit Rana.

The inclusion of 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi completes the lineup. The teenager, who broke Chris Gayle's record for most sixes in an IPL season with 72 and scored 776 runs at a strike rate of 237 for the Rajasthan Royals, will be part of all three squads — Ireland, England, and the Asian Games. If he makes his debut in Belfast on June 26, he will become the youngest man to represent India in senior international cricket, younger than Sachin Tendulkar was in 1989.

## Who Is Missing — and Why

The notable absentees tell their own story. Suryakumar Yadav, who captained India to the T20 World Cup title earlier this year, has been dropped entirely after a poor run of form — 242 runs in nine World Cup innings, 270 in 13 IPL matches. Hardik Pandya, nursing a back injury from the latter stages of the IPL, has been left out of the Asian Games squad but retained for the Afghanistan ODIs, subject to fitness clearance. Kuldeep Yadav, one of India's premier white-ball spinners, has been omitted from every squad, effectively ruling him out of all upcoming overseas assignments.

Shubman Gill, who captains the Test and ODI sides, does not feature in any T20I list. The split is now formal: Gill in Tests and ODIs, Iyer in T20Is, with the selectors showing no interest in an all-format captain.

## What It Means for NRIs

For the Indian diaspora in Japan — one of the fastest-growing NRI communities in Asia, with an estimated 46,000 Indians now living in the country — the Asian Games will be an opportunity to watch Bumrah in person without the chaos and cost of an India-Australia series or an IPL final. The Aichi prefecture is accessible from Tokyo by bullet train, and the T20 format means each match is a single-session commitment.

India's schedule at the Asian Games has not been finalized yet, but the men's cricket tournament will feature 10 teams. India's group-stage opponents will be drawn in the coming weeks. The knockout rounds are expected to run from September 30 to October 3.

**India squad for 2026 Asian Games:** Shreyas Iyer (C), Tilak Varma (VC), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (WK), Ishan Kishan (WK), Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
